cands.name: Vernetta Alston
cands.bio: Durham Democrat and attorney. Former staff attorney with N.C. Prisoner Legal Services and the Center for Death Penalty Litigation. Served on the Durham City Council from 2017 to 2020. Appointed to the N.C. House (District 29) in April 2020 and has held the seat since.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina (listed among 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations)
Equality NC, The People's Alliance and The Independent Weekly (2017 Durham City Council race)

cands.gaps: We found no documented stances or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, immigration enforcement or H-1B, campaign-finance pledges, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site says she helped pass the Unfair Real Estate Agreements act and has worked on housing policy. We could not read any bill record confirming her role, so we left it out. The list of bills she sponsored did not load on the page we read. As a city council member she supported a $95 million affordable housing bond, per Wikipedia. That does not match any of the issues we track, so we did not use it. Her exact district residence and her stated positions in the current campaign were not available.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says she was born in Durham and grew up in Cary, and her campaign site says she was born in Durham and has spent her entire life in the Triangle.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney who worked as a staff attorney on the Racial Justice Act Study, at N.C. Prisoner Legal Services and at the Center for Death Penalty Litigation. Durham City Council member 2017-2020. N.C. House member since April 2020, with Appropriations, Judiciary and Local Government assignments in 2023-24.
qual.why: She has held legislative office for about six years, plus two years on city council, and has a law career. Committee seats were not counted toward the score.
